title: FRL Discrete Gestures: Hand Gesture Recognition from Surface Electromyography
description: This dataset comprises wrist-based surface electromyography (sEMG) recordings from 100 participants performing nine discrete hand gestures (four thumb swipes, four finger-to-thumb pinches, and one thumb tap) for gesture-based human-computer interaction. Recorded using a 16-channel sEMG research device at 2000 Hz, the dataset contains 1900 prompted gesture trials with event annotations and electrode coordinates. The data supports development of generic, user-independent gesture classification models for real-time control of AR/VR interfaces, mobile devices, and accessibility applications.
methods_description: Participants performed prompted discrete hand gestures on their dominant wrist while wearing a 16-channel sEMG research device (sEMG-RD) with dry gold-plated differential electrode pairs. The device sampled at 2000 Hz with 12-bit resolution and ±6.6 mV dynamic range. Gestures were cued via visual prompts in randomized order with variable inter-gesture intervals across 16 recording stages per session. Preprocessing included 40 Hz high-pass filtering and clock drift correction.
